analysis:
This PR is documentation-only in the supplied units. Three items matter for the cache threat model.

(1) docs/architecture/security/encryption.md lines 110-118 add two cache-key behaviours. Ad hoc builds get no persistent cache key, so SSD stores are refused with key_unavailable unless an ephemeral key is explicitly allowed. DEBUG builds can derive the KEK from DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE, a file-based key outside the Secure Enclave. This is the basis of the T-041 finding. The code (SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift) is not supplied, so release-build exclusion and file permission or ownership validation are unverified.

(2) The docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md patch excerpt (changed range 129-153, only partly visible and not an input unit) says SSD eligibility is default-on for the locally selected EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp (PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel). That widens the default-on at-rest cache gate T-041 says needs review. It also says GLM stays outside registered coordinator serving models. The supplied head text for lines 445-881 contains no security-relevant changes.

(3) docs/design/glm53-flash-native.md is new, and only its metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied. It pins artifacts by revision and says glm5_next stays excluded from EngineV2SupportedModels. The release gates are not verified here, and artifact and weight-integrity concerns (T-012, T-027) were not examined.

No code, auth, attestation or coordinator changes are visible. The GLM native code, full-state codec and cache gate need review in a source pass.

findings.detail: The encryption doc now describes a DEBUG-build path where the SSD cache KEK is derived from an operator-created file (`DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE`). That file is protected only by ownership, mode 0600 and volume encryption, not the Secure Enclave. T-041 and its KEK-wipe, HMAC-lookup and at-rest mitigations assume the KEK is rooted in the Secure Enclave. A local process or operator that reads the file can decrypt DBK3 prompt-derived KV artifacts and recompute the HMAC lookup keys, which undercuts the leak-#2 closure. The doc says release builds do not contain this path, but the implementation (`SSDDebugCacheKeyFile.swift`) is not in the supplied evidence, so that claim is unverified. T-041 and its detection hints should record this as a build-gated weaker key-custody mode. A release-build compile-out check and a test that a release binary ignores the env var should also be required.
findings.title: Debug cache-KEK-from-file path is not reflected in the cache threat model
